summary: Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, Zhejiang University as a professor (attested 2015), and the University of Tokyo as a JSPS postdoctoral fellow (attested 2015).
Huawen Bai (1930–2021) was a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Peking University from circa 1951 to 1955 and served as a professor there from circa 1955 to 1998.

Hubert Decleer (1940–2021) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Regent Hotel and Technical School, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte (1975). He later held academic directorship and advisory roles at the School for International Training.

Hubert Durt (1936–2018) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte. He served as professor and editor-in-chief at the EFEO (~1970–2001), director of the Hōbōgirin Institute (~1981–2001), and professor at the ICPBS (~2001–2010).

Hugh B. Urban (born 1968) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1993–1998) studying under Wendy Doniger, Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart, and became an associate professor at Ohio State University (~1998).

Hugh Edward Richardson (1905–2000) was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Keble College (~1924–1927). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1928–1950), founded the Tibet Society and the Institute of Tibetan Studies, Tring, and was an Honorary Fellow at Keble College.
Hugh Gray (1916–2002) was a scholar in Indology who studied at Battersea Grammar School. He served as a lecturer at SOAS and the University of London from circa 1964 to 1982.

Hugh J. Silverman (1945–2013) was a philosopher who earned his doctorate at Stanford University (~1969–1973). He became a professor at Stony Brook University in 1974 and served as executive director of the International Association for Philosophy and Literature (~1976–2013).

Hugo David is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2012, studying with traditional teachers. He held a Newton Fellowship at Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member of EFEO in 2015.

Hugo Makibi Enomiya-Lassalle (1898–1990) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post at Sophia University from circa 1935 to 1970 and studied under traditional teacher Kōun Yamada from circa 1968 to 1989.
Hui-tzu Lu is a scholar in Sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Jing-shen Tao and with traditional teachers Zhiru Shi and Zhihui Shi (attested 2003).
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).
Huifeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2007) and held a post at The University of Hong Kong.

Huimin (born 1954) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He served as a professor at Taipei National University of the Arts, executive director at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and president of DILA (2014–2022).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kuo-wei Liu, also studying under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kirill Solonin, also studying under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Dongguk University (attested 1996).
Hung-Yi Yang is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon.

Huston Smith (1919–2016) was a scholar of religion and philosophy who earned his BA at Central Methodist and PhD at the University of Chicago. He taught at Washington University, MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse University (1973–1983), and UC Berkeley (~1983–1999).

Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where thesis advisers included Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2010).
